stage1.impression: A strong idea, eight glowing cabinets in a spectrum along a wet quay under a concrete wall, but it reads as a render: the wall carries one smooth left-to-right rainbow gradient instead of eight light washes, the horns on top are dark ghost boxes that vanish into the wall, and a dead black band cuts the frame between the quay and the river. Surfaces look denoiser-smeared, the cabinet interiors blow out to white, and the puddle reflections are clean mirrored rectangles that look pasted on.

blocking_9: Eight distinct tall coloured washes on the wall, brightest above each speaker and blending only where they overlap. Right now the space between speakers is brighter than the wall above them.
Each speaker reads whole: the horn's silhouette and edges separate from the wall behind it.
No crushed black band between the quay and the water. The quay edge and the river read as surfaces.
Cabinet interiors keep their colour without clipping to white.
Concrete texture is crisp and free of denoiser blotches, and the board-form lines and tie holes are legible at full size.
Reflections in the wet paving and the river are broken up by real surface variation instead of mirror copies.

defects.what: The wall wash is one continuous horizontal rainbow gradient. Eight washes do not read. The column between speakers 4 and 5 (690-760) is brighter at 74.8 than the column above speaker 4 (600-700) at 67.4.
The horns are dark, low-contrast boxes (lum median 20-35, range 10-23) that merge with the wall. The product does not read whole.
A dead black band across the full width at the quay edge, lum median 2.4 with 66% crushed.
The Ember cabinet interior clips (10.9% clipped) and shifts toward pink-white. Ice (760-825) clips 8.8%.
Denoiser smearing and blotchy low-frequency noise on the concrete. Its texture reads soft and painted.
The reflections in the wet paving are near-perfect mirrored rectangles of the cabinets, too clean for wet granite.
The river reflections are vertically smeared copies with little ripple structure.
The frame ends fall to near black (lum 10). The wall's extent and the opera-house scale are lost at the sides.
Eight identical models at identical spacing and angle read as a CG array, although this is the line-up's intent.

changes.problem: The uplights spill a 120-degree cone sideways, so the wall gets one smeared gradient and eight washes never form.

evidence.measured: Above speaker 4 (600-700) lum median 67.4. Between speakers 4 and 5 (690-760) lum median 74.8. The horizontal profile is a single smooth hump (27-82-24) with no eight-peak structure.

change.to: spread_deg 55, target [x, 2.6, 3.4] (aimed back at the wall face, position unchanged under each speaker)

changes.expected: Eight tall coloured columns on the wall, about 0.8-1.2 m wide at their base, rising to the coping and overlapping only above about 2.5 m. Peak above each speaker at least 1.4x the trough between speakers.

changes.problem: The wall face sits 2.6 m behind the speakers, too far for the light leaving each cabinet to make a tight, tall wash.

evidence.measured: Trough between washes lum 74.8 against peaks around 67. The washes have fully merged by mid-height (vertical profile 48-73-53).

changes.expected: The washes stay distinct, with darker concrete between them, and the wall feels closer and more monumental behind the row.

changes.problem: The horns on top of the cabinets get no light and disappear into the wall, so the speakers do not read whole.

evidence.measured: Horn regions lum median 20-35 with lum range 10-23. Smoke's horn (1175-1245) has median 20.3, close to the wall behind it.

changes.expected: Each horn shows a cool rim on its top edge and right side and separates from the coloured wall. The horn region p95 rises above 70.

changes.problem: The quay edge and the near water render as a crushed black strip that cuts the frame in two.

change.to: water z -0.04, curb #8A8780 roughness 0.25, so the curb face is a thin lit edge and the river starts right at the quay.

changes.expected: The black band shrinks to a thin dark line. The river and its coloured reflections start directly under the quay.

changes.problem: The cabinet interiors clip to white and lose their colour, especially Ember and Ice.

change.to: 200. c1's narrower cone puts more of the light on the wall, which keeps the washes bright.

changes.expected: The interiors keep saturated colour with highlight detail. Clipping falls below 3% per cabinet.

changes.problem: The puddle reflections are mirror copies, which reads as CG rather than wet granite.

evidence.measured: Visually, sharp rectangular cabinet reflections with no breakup. The region spans lum 9-217.

change.setting: set.props.3 paving wet / puddle_m, and set.props.5 ripple

changes.expected: The paving reflections break into patchy wet and dry areas. The river reflections become long broken streaks.

changes.problem: The concrete reads soft and blotchy from denoising at a low sample count, and the board-form texture is lost.

evidence.measured: Visually, low-frequency mottling on the wall with soft board lines. The top band (0 0 1440 60) has lum range only 38.

change.to: render at full 2880x1200, 1024 samples, OpenImageDenoise with albedo and normal passes (prefilter accurate), and haze density 0.012 cut to 0.007

changes.expected: Board seams, tie holes and aggregate are crisp. The wall's top band gains local contrast.

changes.problem: The ends of the frame drop to near black, so the wall's monumental extent and the riverside setting do not read.

evidence.measured: Left end lum median 8.7. The right end (1280-1440) is 10.2.

change.to: sky strength 0.12; far-shore glow emit 1.2, so the river picks up distant warm points at the ends

changes.expected: The ends sit around lum 18-25 with legible concrete and faint water sparkle, still well below the speakers.

out_of_scope.request: Let light glow through the upper cabinet and horn so the top half reads.
out_of_scope.why: The batts and the horn are fixed. The cabinet must stop light where it really would, so the top can only be revealed by external light (c3).

out_of_scope.request: Vary each speaker's angle or spacing to break the CG-array look.
out_of_scope.why: The speaker positions are listed as the product instances and the uplight placement is fixed under each one. Changing the row is a framing and product decision for the owner.
